support_bodies.name: west Z-seam slide-head catch
support_bodies.rationale: The flat underside of the -X rail's slide head - the Z seam's one down-looking face, and the whole of the screwless bottom-to-top joint's bearing against lift. Lifting a seated back-top lands its foot's flat top face on this one along the rail's whole run; pitching the catch would turn it into a cam and give that full-face bearing up. Its two interface islands are the one run either side of the PRV passage, the 12 mm opening that has to cross this flank, and that same opening is what lets the body root on the bed outside the flank instead of on the arm's own under-flare.

support_bodies.name: east Z-seam slide-head catch
support_bodies.rationale: The +X rail's slide head, the mirror of the west catch and continuous over its whole run because nothing crosses this flank. With no opening through the wall beside it the body has no lane to the bed, so it roots on the arm's own 45 degree under-flare 8.00 mm below the catch it carries. It and front-bottom's pair are the three material-rooted supports in the box and the only bodies outside the 15 mm band.

support_bodies.name: ASSE anchor aft round-section soffit and west ceiling-strip tree
support_bodies.rationale: The first contact is the flat underside of the anchor's aft round section, east of where its 45 degree corbel stops. That corbel is struck on the deepest section's V foot and carries the anchor's underside from the -X wall out to that foot; each round section is a box running on east to the chain's own axis with the fitting's bore cut out of its east face, so 8.5 mm of flat soffit stands past the foot with nothing under it. Taking it back would take material out from under the bore that seats the fitting, and the V foot is already as far east as a wall-rooted wedge on this anchor can reach. The -X fixed ceiling strip's underside over the chain joins the same bed-rooted body through the open enclosure: that strip's own 45 degree corbel is deepest at the flank and thinnest at the removable panel's edge, and the chain stands in the run band the corbel has to give up.

support_bodies.name: forward west service-furniture and ceiling-strip tree
support_bodies.rationale: The -X wall's service contacts through the water-split and flow-regulator band, and the -X ceiling strip's fore end at the Y-seam mouth. Each keeps a component, routing, anchor or seam-clearance lane open on the wall it stands beside; their eight interfaces share one bed-rooted tree in the open enclosure, so none of them hides a separate short or material-rooted support.

support_bodies.name: core-hold, drip-sleeve, dock, nameplate and rear-wall tree
support_bodies.rationale: The two first contacts carry the west and east cold-core aft hold-down soffits over the core's insertion lane - a pillar in that lane blocks the core riding in through the Y-seam mouth, and the bearing face is the lowest thing on each bracket. Eleven more contacts join the same bed-rooted body through the open enclosure: the ASSE drip-pan sleeve's floor east of its wall-rooted 20 mm corbel (the tray is longer than a wedge off that one wall can carry, and nothing stands under its east half to root a second); the magnetic pogo dock's pocket roof in that sleeve's backstop, the flat the male pill's flange seats under, whose mouth has to open east so the pill goes in from the bench; the anchor's fore round-section soffit, the mirror of tree-1's; the nameplate mouth's ceiling in the +Y wall; the keystone jack's retention ceiling; three of the five Wago-well retention ceilings; the C14 tunnel's aperture ceiling, the bridge the bore's width between the block's two flanks; the +X wall's service contact behind the PSU; and the -X ceiling strip's aft end at the water bulkhead.

support_bodies.name: east Wago-well and fixed ceiling-strip tree
support_bodies.rationale: Two of the five Wago-well retention ceilings on the +X wall. Each well grips its lever nut against the wall and that ceiling is the face which holds it in, so opening it into a 45 degree roof gives the retention up. Both exposed regions of the +X fixed ceiling strip join the same bed-rooted body: its underside over the raised relay, where the strip's corbel is already given up across that complete band, and its fore-end crown at the Y-seam mouth, where front-top's ceiling tongue lands one slip under it.

support_bodies.name: west lower Y-seam socket collar crown
support_bodies.rationale: The complete crown of the lower west Y-seam socket collar. It keeps the collar's full structural stock over the cross-pin's square slide slot and its blind heat-set pocket, so the pin registers on a square pass envelope and the M3 bears on a whole section; pitching the crown into a roof would erase that envelope. Its one tree grows from the bed through the open cavity.

support_bodies.name: west Z-seam slide-head catch
support_bodies.rationale: The flat underside of the -X rail's slide head - the Z seam's one down-looking face, and the whole of the screwless bottom-to-top joint's bearing against lift. Lifting a seated front-top lands its foot's flat top face on this one along the rail's entire run, and pitching the catch would turn it into a cam. The arm under it already returns to the wall on a 45 degree under-flare, so there is no wall-rooted wedge left to grow, and nothing crosses this flank at the catch's height to give the body a lane to the bed: it roots on that under-flare 8.00 mm below the catch. It, its east mirror and back-bottom's east catch are the three material-rooted supports in the box and the only bodies outside the 15 mm band, and they are what the campaign owes its next fix.

support_bodies.name: X- pump boss-bearing shoulder
support_bodies.rationale: The flat annular shoulder bears axially on the fitted pump boss while the complete octagonal wall locates X, Y and yaw. Chamfering the shoulder would trade away bearing area rather than remove an accidental overhang; its centre bore remains open for direct support removal.
